newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on seeding delay concern.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on seeding delay concern.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on talk about delays in seeding of the U.S. winter wheat crop due to forecasts for heavy rains this week accompanied by cool weather, traders said.
"Wet and cold also will delay wheat plantings as well as delay corn harvest," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Meteorologists early Wednesday said widespread rain was forecast for the U.S. central Plains and Midwest the rest of the week which should delay winter wheat planting.
Support also came from news this week USDA Secretary Dan Glickman was in favor of subsidizing U.S. wheat exports if necessary, they said.

Wheat also was buoyed by talk Sparks Companies issued a forecast this week indicating that USDA's quarterly stocks report Monday will show U.S. wheat stocks at 1.716 billion bushels, which would be a record low.
Sparks officials were unavailable for comment.
Gains were limited by profit taking. Wheat had rallied Monday and again Tuesday and was due for an occasional profit taking setback, traders said.
Wheat closed unchanged to three cents per bushel higher, with December unchanged at $4.29-1/2.

Technicians early Wednesday cited initial resistance in the December contract at $4.33-1/2 and second resistance at $442.00. First support in the December was at $4.25.00 and second support at $4.16-1/2.

Wheat was also supported by commercial and fund buying with the purchases ranging mostly under one half million bushels each, traders said. Refco Inc sold two million bushels of December, sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, down from 16,229 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
Wheat options trading featured Smith Barney's sale of 300 March $4.40 puts at 32 to 33 cents, traders said.
Options volume was estimated at 3,000 contracts, down from 5,828 Tuesday.
